safety_baseline.description: No current worse report and no negative response (worse, stopped or worsening) in this episode that a sourced rule has resolved. An older negative stays unresolved until a profile defines a sourced resolution rule.
The episode's full exposure history is available. Truncated history could hide a negative response, so it is never evidence of safety and no profile may remove this requirement.
At least one exposure to this policy's reviewed work for the current stage, with stated demand, performed as shown. This is the minimum needed to evaluate a transition, not a readiness criterion.
The latest reviewed exposure did not feel worse during the work. An unreported or unsure answer is unknown, never a pass.
The next-day response to the latest reviewed exposure is known and not worse. This mirrors the scheduler's existing delayed-response hold.

functional_checkpoints.description: Walks with a normal stride without pain.
functional_checkpoints.required_input: Per-injury report: can you walk at a normal stride without pain? (yes / no / not sure)

functional_checkpoints.description: Jogs at very low speed without pain.
functional_checkpoints.required_input: Per-injury report after an optional, explicitly offered low-speed jog: pain during / after (better / same / worse / not tried)

functional_checkpoints.description: A submaximal resisted isometric contraction of the injured tissue is pain-free.
functional_checkpoints.required_input: Per-injury report captured with a reviewed isometric exposure: was the hold pain-free? (yes / no / not sure)

families.description: Acute muscle or musculotendinous strain: protect, restore pain-free movement, progressively load, then speed and sport demands.
Ligament sprain and symptomatic joint instability: protected movement, control and balance, progressive loading, then reactive and sport demands.
Tendon pain and tendinopathy: load management through isometric, then heavier slow, then energy-storage loading.
Painful joint irritation or impingement: settle symptoms, restore range and control, then load through tolerated range.
Joint hyperextension trauma: structural injury screened first, then protected range and end-range control before loading.
Direct-blow muscle or soft-tissue bruise: protect early, restore range, then progressive loading.
Symptom reports without a tissue diagnosis (pain, soreness, tightness, stiffness, swelling): symptom-led, conservative, no diagnosis implied.

prescriptions.instructions: Protect the strained area and avoid movements that aggravate it. During the first 2 to 3 days, rest from exercise that loads it. Use comfortable everyday movement; do not force a stretch or add resisted chest work.
stop_when: Stop if pain prevents comfortable movement or symptoms worsen.
Seek help for severe or worsening pain, swelling or inability to use the area.

prescriptions.instructions: Sit with the affected lower leg supported and the foot free to move. Slowly move the ankle a small amount upwards and downwards around a comfortable middle range. Do not force pointing the toes, deep upward bending, a loaded knee-over-toe lunge or a stretch into a pinch. Keep the movement unweighted and controlled; follow any clinician-directed movement restriction. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.

prescriptions.instructions: Reduce provoking forceful elbow straightening, repetitive throwing, heavy triceps work and pressing. Rest from activities that reproduce the pinch and follow individual restrictions. Persistent catching, locking or a mechanical block needs assessment rather than repeated attempts to force movement. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.
stop_when: Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.

prescriptions.instructions: Sit with the affected upper arm by your side and the forearm comfortably supported. With the hand empty, slowly bend and straighten the elbow through a small comfortable range. Stop short of a pinch and do not force full straightening, rotate against resistance, perform a large end-range CAR or add weight. Stop and seek assessment for catching, locking or a blocked movement. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.

prescriptions.instructions: Reduce provoking grip, pushing through the hand, loaded wrist extension and repetitive wrist compression. Rest the wrist in a comfortable supported position and follow clinician-directed splint or immobilization advice without changing it. Do not perform band distraction, push-ups, resisted side-to-side holds or force range to clear a pinch. The subtype and safe release from protection are not captured, so automatic wrist movement and loading remain unavailable. Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.
stop_when: Stop if symptoms worsen during or after the movement. Seek assessment for catching, locking, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot swollen joint or fever.

prescriptions.instructions: Protect the affected toe from being bent backwards again. Pause provoking push-off, tiptoe work, running and jumping. Rest the foot in a comfortable supported position. Follow any individually prescribed footwear, walking support or weight-bearing restriction without changing it. The affected toe, joint stability and injury grade need assessment before toe curls, stretching or loaded forefoot work; this guidance does not diagnose turf toe. Stop automatic rehab and seek assessment for giving way, locking, suspected instability, deformity, major swelling or loss of joint use. Seek urgent help for altered sensation, a cold or blue limb, or symptoms suggesting a fracture, dislocation or tear. Follow clinician restrictions. If symptoms worsen, stop the provoking activity and seek assessment rather than testing the joint.

prescriptions.instructions: Protect the injured finger from being pulled or bent backwards. Avoid gripping against resistance, catching impacts and contact work. Rest the hand comfortably supported. Follow any hand-therapist splint or strapping instructions exactly; do not change the finger position, undo the splint for app exercises or decide when to stop wearing it. Finger exercises need the assessed injury and individual protection plan; no automatic stretching or finger holds are prescribed. prescriptions.instructions: Protect the elbow from repeat over-straightening. Pause pressing, throwing, forceful lockout and resisted elbow work. prescriptions.instructions: Protect the wrist from being bent backwards again and from weight through the palm or knuckles. Pause pushing, loaded wrist extension and heavy grip work. prescriptions.instructions: Protect the injured hand from repeated backward bending, forceful gripping and contact impacts. Support the hand comfortably at rest and avoid using it to bear body weight. Follow any individually prescribed hand protection and movement restrictions.
